headline: Chips Drag, Healthcare Holds — Traders Weigh Geopolitical Noise Ahead of Tuesday's Open
body_html:
Wall Street enters Tuesday on a cautious footing after Monday's session delivered a split verdict: 275 stocks in our universe closed higher against 261 that fell, a near-even tally that masked a brutal day for semiconductor-related names. The chip sector surrendered 3.22%, the worst performance across any group, while Semtech and Ichor Holdings shed more than 9% apiece and Coherent and MaxLinear fell sharply alongside them. Homebuilders also struggled, dropping 1.44%, as rate-sensitive names stayed under pressure.

Away from those trouble spots, pockets of genuine strength emerged. Healthcare gained 0.59%, Energy added 0.55%, and Consumer names edged 0.45% higher. Fair Isaac surged nearly 11% to lead all gainers, while Victoria's Secret rose 6.9% and Manhattan Associates climbed 6.3%. The moves suggest investors are selectively rotating toward earnings-visibility names rather than abandoning equities outright.

Overnight, macro currents are mixed. The IMF flagged that artificial-intelligence investment is supporting global growth but warned that debt and conflict remain threats to the outlook. Middle East tensions linger after Houthi missile activity disrupted Saudi airports. Oil has softened on news of potential Russian diesel supply relief, a development worth watching as energy traders settle in for Tuesday's session.

briefs.headline: Visa Clears Hurdle for China Domestic Payments Push
briefs.body: Regulators have approved Visa to begin preparations for operating a domestic card business inside China, a milestone that opens a long-sought market for the payments giant. The development marks a meaningful step in what has been a decades-long effort to access Chinese consumer spending directly.

briefs.headline: IMF: AI Spending Lifts Growth, but Debt and War Cloud the Picture
briefs.body: The International Monetary Fund credits a surge in artificial-intelligence investment with underpinning global economic momentum, but its latest assessment warns that elevated sovereign debt and ongoing armed conflicts pose significant downside risks. The dual message sets a complicated backdrop for risk assets as earnings season accelerates.

briefs.headline: Saudi Airport Attacks Roil Regional Air Travel
briefs.body: Qatar Airways has suspended flights to Riyadh and Dammam after Houthi strikes disrupted airport operations, while a Saudi-led coalition confirmed it intercepted a ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh. Reports indicate warning systems failed to alert before the initial deadly strikes, heightening regional security concerns.

briefs.headline: Oil Eases as Russian Diesel Prospects Offset Gulf Disruption Premium
briefs.body: Crude prices retreated overnight as prospects for increased Russian diesel supply appeared to temper the risk premium built in around Middle Eastern tensions. A separate report noted the Americas are sitting on a glut of heavy oil due to freight bottlenecks, while Asian and European buyers scramble for available barrels.

briefs.headline: Salesforce Earns a Rare Double Upgrade as SaaS Fears Fade
briefs.body: A prominent analyst firm lifted its rating on Salesforce by two notches, arguing that widespread fears of a structural collapse in software-as-a-service valuations were misplaced. The upgrade is drawing attention ahead of the open as investors reassess beaten-down enterprise software names in a choppy tape.

briefs.headline: India Stocks Flat as Firmer Inflation Dims Rate-Cut Hopes
briefs.body: Indian equity indices opened little changed Tuesday after the latest domestic inflation reading came in stronger than expected, reinforcing the case for the Reserve Bank of India to hold rates rather than ease. The data adds to a broader emerging-market theme of central banks constrained by persistent price pressures.
